newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Italy's Prodi to back troops in visit to Albania.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi to back troops in visit to Albania.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi was set to visit Albania on Sunday to underline his support for an Italian-led multinational force that will protect the distribution of aid to the volatile Balkan state.
Prodi would meet President Sali Berisha in Tirana to discuss the deployment of 2,500 Italian troops, the bulk of an eight-nation mission, from Tuesday, officials said.
He was due to give a news conference in Tirana at 1200 GMT after paying his first visit to the rebel-held southern port of Vlore, according to officials and state television.

Advance troops of the United Nations-approved 6,000-strong mission have deployed in Albania to plot the arrival of the main force, which will include soldiers from France, Spain, Greece, Turkey, Austria, Denmark and Romania.

A 20-strong Italian unit that landed on Friday in Vlore, the scene of much recent violence, received a friendly welcome, although the situation there was "far from normal", the state-run news agency ATA said. It said gunfire rang out there in the afternoon and evening.

The multinational force will aim to distribute emergency food and medicines to the cities, hit by near-anarchy after get-rich-quick investment schemes collapsed, officials said. Newspapers put the death toll from six weeks of unrest at 279.
Soldiers belonging to the force will have the right to defend themselves if they are attacked while distributing aid in Albania, Italy's Defence Minister Beniamino Andreatta said.

"If there are attacks during the distribution of aid, the only means to guarantee results is the use of arms," he said during a brief trip to Tirana. "Weapons will be used for self-protection," he added.
Some 3,500 Albanian troops, including commandos and tank brigades, will help the multinational mission, officials said.

Prodi, who won parliamentary backing for the mission at the cost of a split with his hard-left allies, said he hoped "elections (in Albania) would happen quickly and that one month after the vote we can begin to bring our troops back".
Andreatta said a final decision would be taken in Rome on Monday assigning troops from each country to key locations across Albania.
Albanian Defence Minister Shaqir Vukaj said his country ran no risk of slipping into civil war.
"There is no basis for civil war in Albania because in history Albanians have not killed each other for regional, religious or political reasons," he said.
King Leka I, who returned home from exile in South Africa to a tumultuous welcome from nearly 2,000 supporters, said restoration of the monarchy could unify the Balkan state.
Speaking shortly after landing in the country he left as an infant, he said the turmoil had come about because Albanians had their political will denied for more than 50 years.
"I hope I am a unifying factor, a factor that can bring together all the diverse political and religious and national hopes," he said.
King Leka, 58, was only a few days old when his father, King Zog, fled the country with his family in 1939.
He gave guarded support to the multinational mission.
"As long as they come here with good will, on a mission of peace, I welcome them," he said. "But should there be any action to change the situation, we will have to give that a second thought."

In Italy, U.N. Secretary General Koffi Annan said he believed the mission was crucial. "To the soldiers about to go, I want to say that they have a difficult task ahead of them but one of great importance and honour," he said.

A French naval vessel with around 120 men aboard was expected to leave the Italian port of Brindisi over the weekend for a reconnaissance mission in the western port of Durres, where a 20-strong Italian advance unit landed on Friday.
Two Spanish naval ships were due to arrive in Brindisi on Sunday.
The U.N. World Food Programme said a first aid shipment had left the Italian port of Trieste with some 400 tonnes of food aid destined for Durres. It was due to arrive on Tuesday morning.
